text: tage_compare_groups() friends implement statistical models paper’s clock analyses; R Python packages agree numerically. Elastic net clocks compared estimated marginal-mean contrasts value ~ group + covariates (emmeans lm); Bayesian ridge clocks go REML meta-regression (metafor::rma.uni) weights sample prediction standard deviation reports z-tests. One row per contrast, estimate always meaning group2 - group1, plus se, 95% interval ci_low / ci_high, statistic, df, p_value, p_adjusted label holding usual *** ** * ^ stars. Two figures built directly tests, return statistics "tage_stats" attribute: Every figure drawn theme_tage() one set colour tokens (tage_colors()), Python package: groups take colour-vision-safe categorical slots fixed order reference group grey (tage_series_colors()), clock outcome keeps colour across figures, signed effects use one blue–grey–red scale centred zero, text never wears data colour. Add theme_tage() ggplots match. ggplot carries size , figure functions record size designed grow number clocks, modules panels. tage_save_plot() uses size; tage_fig_size() reads back knitr chunk: variance_strata chooses whether residual variance comes two compared groups ("subset") every group stratum ("all_data"); p_adjust_scope chooses correction family — "within_column" across comparisons strata one clock, "across_columns" across clocks modules within comparison stratum, "global". tage_boxplot() uses engine default (stat_method = "emmeans"); pass stat_method = "t.test" (another ggpubr::stat_compare_means method) plain two-sample test.
